_comment: A worked scene. Copy this, replace every value with your own, keep the keys. Keys starting with _ are ignored. Run `build_prompt.py <shot> --slots --scene this.json` to see which extra keys a particular shot needs.
_subject_kind: person (default), animal, bird or object. It selects the vocabulary for framing, pronouns, the anti-frozen clause and what identity preserves. Only person was ever tested - see references/subjects.md. An object kind also requires AMBIENT.
SUBJECT_DEFINITION: the young woman in <Picture 1>: long wavy ginger-red hair, fair skin with light freckles, wearing a cream short-sleeve t-shirt, a dark cord necklace with a metal cross pendant, high-waisted blue jeans with a brown leather belt, and woven cord wrist wraps on both wrists
ENVIRONMENT_ELEMENTS: dark rocky cliffs, patches of green aurora borealis in the sky, still water, and an old wooden sailing ship with tall masts
LIGHTING: cold blue-green arctic lighting with the aurora glowing softly overhead
GEAR: an ARRI Alexa with a Cooke Varotal 18-100mm zoom lens
PERFORMANCE: expression shifts from blank and neutral into dawning realization and slight shock: her eyes widen and focus more intensely, her brow lifts and tightens, her lips part slightly, and her breathing grows visibly shallower and faster, the change building through the middle of the shot and settling into a held, wide-eyed stillness by the end
SOUNDSCAPE: A faint cold wind continues throughout, with distant creaking from the ship's rigging
MUSIC: A single sustained low string note swells partway through the shot, then fades toward the end
_shot_specific: The keys below are only needed by some shots. Harmless to leave in.
NEAR_OBJECTS: the trunks of two near pines
_multi_subject: whip-pan needs SUBJECT_2. rack-focus needs SUBJECT_2 and SUBJECT_3. Wire the plates in the same order, because <Picture N> is positional.
SUBJECT_2_DEFINITION: the woman in <Picture 2>: shoulder-length dark hair, olive skin, wearing a heavy charcoal wool coat over a grey roll-neck
SUBJECT_3_DEFINITION: the woman in <Picture 3>: short blonde hair, pale skin, wearing a rust-orange padded jacket
_split_screen: split-screen needs these four. It also needs a scene where one action reads from three angles.
ACTION: seated at a cluttered desk typing on a keyboard, a bright monitor in front of her, a mug and scattered papers beside it, a dark room and a rain-streaked window behind her
PANEL_1_ANGLE: her from her left side in profile as she types
PANEL_2_ANGLE: the front, framed over the back of the monitor with the screen glow on her face
PANEL_3_ANGLE: her from behind in full, her back and the bright monitor in view
_direction: Optional. Only the defaults were tested - see references/direction.md. PAN_DIRECTION: right|left (whip-pan). ROLL_DIRECTION: counterclockwise|clockwise (dutch-angle).
_object_only: AMBIENT is required when SUBJECT_KIND is object: what moves in the scene while the subject stays inert, e.g. "the grass, the spray and the racing cloud".
